def _insight_query_screenshot_width(query: dict) -> ScreenWidth:
    """Initial viewport width for an insight-style query render.

    Only left-to-right funnels (vertical layout, which is the default) need the wide
    viewport — they grow horizontally with step count. Top-to-bottom funnels (horizontal
    layout) grow vertically, not horizontally. Small funnels are constrained later by the
    width measurement. The higher the number, the more RAM the Chromium driver needs.

    A metric renders as a card whose height derives from the viewport width, so a narrower
    viewport keeps it at dashboard-tile size instead of a 400px-tall banner.
    Mirrors the frontend's check (InsightVizNode wrapper required), which gates the
    metric card CSS — a bare TrendsQuery gets neither, so it must keep the default viewport.
    """
    source = query.get("source", query)  # This to handle the InsightVizNode wrapper
    is_funnel = source.get("kind") == NodeKind.FUNNELS_QUERY
    funnels_filter = source.get("funnelsFilter") or {}
    funnel_layout = funnels_filter.get("layout")
    is_left_to_right_funnel = is_funnel and (funnel_layout is None or funnel_layout == FunnelLayout.VERTICAL)
    if is_left_to_right_funnel:
        return 4000

    trends_filter = source.get("trendsFilter") or {}
    is_metric = (
        query.get("kind") == NodeKind.INSIGHT_VIZ_NODE
        and source.get("kind") == NodeKind.TRENDS_QUERY
        and trends_filter.get("display") == ChartDisplayType.METRIC
    )
    return 600 if is_metric else 800

                page.wait_for_timeout(500)
            page.screenshot(path=image_path)

design.queryScope: Exact actual trace, fixed UTC [start,end), production resource environment and services mikka-web/mikka-daemon, same as frozen span_timeline.
design.pagination: Canonical raw 500-row pagination remains unchanged. Display pages use consecutive actual UUID sets, eight rows maximum by default (one to eight configurable offline); no display OFFSET.
design.offsets: Compute min(timestamp) OVER () before filtering to selected page UUIDs, so every page shares the full-trace start anchor.
design.order: timestamp, base64 span_id, uuid; preserve existing canonical page order. Do not re-sort decoded hex IDs.
design.returnedColumns: Exactly the displayed seven columns; no raw attributes or hidden message/secret fields.
design.durationFormatting: Milliseconds with three displayed decimal places only. Underlying expected/query numeric receipts retain original precision. Status0 is Unset, not success.
design.sentinelLimit: Expected page length + 1; unexpected extra row rejects that page instead of being hidden.
design.lowerCapacity: If actual pixels clip rows, generate smaller consecutive pages using --rows 1..8. Do not alter server pageSize or export dimensions via invented properties.
design.wideColumns: If a critical string/ID is clipped, reduce the actual SQL projection into paired timing/lineage views of the same UUID page; both must retain span identity and actual stage/service. tableSettings alone is not relied on to hide/reorder columns. Requery and inspect each official PNG.
design.exactDataRequirement: Every page row must match its expected projection from actual canonical metadata. All page identity sets must be disjoint and their union equal the canonical span_timeline IDs. Stage presence and parent integrity remain separate canonical acceptance checks.

permissions.data: Actual Logs/APM query and exporter service access remain untested until a real case; do not infer them from Default/events access or source code.
permissions.insights: Use existing authorized MCP insight create/get/query; only real case-bound new insights or already owned issue targets.
permissions.exports: Use existing trusted runner and numeric insight id, existing export:write/read access and expected-main-SHA gate; no new key or sharing change.
permissions.blocked: Do not retry interrupted browser login, inject cookies, invent connectionId or export_context, change public access, or bypass RBAC.
permissions.uncertainMutation: Do not blindly repeat insight-create/export POST after a timeout with unknown outcome; retain the response/request identity and resolve the existing request first.
